ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners must be screened against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK HMT sanctions, the PBOC anti-money laundering list, SAMR public security adverse database, and FATF-aligned Taiwan financial supervisory databases. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign, domestic, and international organization PEPs, their family members and close associates, require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval, and continuous transaction monitoring. Negative news and sanctions hits must be escalated to the designated AML compliance officer before account opening or registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Autonomous Declaration System (National Enterprise Registration Service Platform)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters. A foreign or English name may be used concurrently but cannot replace the Chinese legal name. The four-tier naming convention is: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry or business scope plus organizational form, e.g., XX (City) XX Co., Ltd. Non-Chinese shareholder names must be transliterated into a phonetically appropriate simplified Chinese sequence. Pure pinyin, Latin abbreviations, or traditional Chinese characters are not acceptable for the legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name declaration is rejected, SAMR will issue a written refusal with the legal basis. The applicant may submit a new autonomous name declaration with a different distinctive trade name, or apply for administrative reconsideration to SAMR within 60 days of service under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, and thereafter file administrative litigation within 15 days after the reconsideration decision. If the refusal concerns a sensitive token, ministerial consent or a pre-approval letter must be obtained and attached to the resubmission. Preserve all online declaration timestamps, screen records, and rejection notices to support the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a LegalTech SaaS WFOE, a virtual office or commercial mailbox-only arrangement is de facto rejected by SAMR, municipal tax authorities, and banks. The registered address must be a fixed commercial premise with actual operations, including staff, computer equipment, server or cloud access, and a physical nameplate. A co-working or incubator address is acceptable only if the WFOE has a genuine direct lease or seat license, the landlord files the lease with the local registry, and the WFOE actually conducts business there during office hours. Banks conduct video or in-person verification; a non-physical mailbox will cause account opening refusal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 35-45% for a newly incorporated WFOE in the first 12 months, rising to 60% if tax filing anomalies or suspicious bank transactions occur, and dropping to about 20% after three years of full compliance. Checklist: (1) office nameplate at the registered address; (2) original lease or property ownership certificate; (3) full-time staff present with ID and labor contracts; (4) office furniture and IT equipment; (5) original business license and corporate seals; (6) tax invoicing software and electronic invoice systems; (7) daily business books and bank statements; (8) social insurance and payroll records; (9) internet and phone lines in the WFOE's name; (10) SaaS platform access logs demonstrating actual business operations. Failure of any item may lead to administrative penalty, deregistration, and bank account freezing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Articles 6, 12, 15, 128, 154, 172, 202 and 370; read together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Article 7, and the Company Registration Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Company Registration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; online filing through the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration and E-Government Service Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation / Articles of Association, filed under Article 6 of the Company Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Taiwan limited company. For a wholly foreign-owned company, the foreign investor must remit the authorized capital into a Taiwan bank account in the company name and the paid-in capital must be verified by a certified public accountant before registration; no blocked escrow account is required by the Company Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD (the Company)
Adopted on [date] at Taipei, Taiwan.

WHEREAS, the Company is a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company formed under the Company Act of the Republic of China; and
WHEREAS, the sole foreign shareholder has validly subscribed for the entire authorized share capital and has caused the capital to be deposited in a Taiwan bank account in the Company's name; and
WHEREAS, all directors duly elected at the incorporation stage have waived notice of this first board meeting and are present, forming a quorum; and
WHEREAS, the Board is vested with the power to complete the statutory incorporation and corporate organization of the Company;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

1. Share Capital Subscription: The Board hereby ratifies the subscription of the issued share capital of the Company in the amount of [amount] divided into [number] ordinary shares, all fully allotted to the founding foreign shareholder, and confirms that the capital received is credited to the Company as paid-in capital free of encumbrances. The Board directs the Company's certified public accountant to issue the mandatory capital verification report and authorizes the Managing Director to sign all share-capital filings required by the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

2. Banking Authorization: The Board adopts the principal banking relationship at a licensed domestic bank selected by the Managing Director and authorizes the opening of corporate operating and foreign-currency accounts in the Company's name. The Board designates the Managing Director, the Corporate Secretary, and the Chief Financial Officer as authorized signatories; any one may sign singly

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA / 国家税务总局); electronic services via the China Electronic Taxpayer (e-Tax) portal accessible at https://tpass.etax.com.cn and the 'Taxpayer Service Platform' for all tax filings, invoice issuance, and registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CN_WFOE_LTD (a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise under PRC law) must first obtain a business license from the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR). After incorporation, within 30 calendar days, the WFOE must complete enterprise tax registration at the competent STA office either through the e-Tax portal or in person. The electronic registration requires the Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC) shown on the business license, the articles of association, legal representative identification, and proof of paid-up capital. Upon successful registration, the STA issues the taxpayer identification number (TIN), which is identical to the USCC. The enterprise must simultaneously register for VAT, corporate income tax, stamp duty, and payroll/social insurance. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Chinese establishment that sells digital services into China, the foreign entity must either obtain a TIN through the streamlined temporary tax registration procedure or appoint a Chinese withholding agent to collect and remit VAT on its behalf.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under Corporate Income Tax; a WFOE cannot elect pass-through or otherwise alter its PRC resident enterprise status. Under VAT, the enterprise may elect to become a general VAT taxpayer (even if annual sales are below the RMB 5 million threshold) to claim input VAT credits, or it may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer subject to the simplified collection rate (currently 1% as of the applicable policy window). No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist in the PRC tax system.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for PRC-established entities; all companies must register for VAT upon incorporation. For non-resident foreign enterprises supplying services to China without physical presence, VAT registration is mandatory when annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 500,000; otherwise a Chinese withholding agent may be designated. An annual taxable sales threshold of RMB 5 million determines mandatory general VAT taxpayer status for domestic entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates a real-time tax-control invoice system. VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-approved invoice management system using the tax authority-certified U-Key. Fully digitalized electronic invoices (FDED) must be reported to the Electronic Invoice Service Platform in near-real-time. Each invoice carries a unique 32-digit invoice number and a tax authority digital signature for anti-fraud authentication. Reconciliation of invoices with the central tax database is mandatory before any input VAT deduction can be claimed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The cloud document automation and e-signature authentication services qualify as 'modern services' (information technology services) under PRC VAT rules and are zero-rated when consumed entirely outside mainland China. To claim zero-rating, the WFOE must demonstrate that: (1) the service recipient is a non-resident enterprise (including a Taiwan-registered legal entity), (2) the service is actually rendered and wholly consumed abroad, (3) the payment is received from abroad in foreign currency or RMB, and (4) the enterprise files the 'Export Services Exemption and Zero-Rate Declaration' with the STA along with supporting contracts. Services supplied to foreign individuals may alternatively be treated as exempt from VAT if they meet the consumption-outside-China test.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Service contract or agreement with the overseas (Taiwan) customer
Bank inward remittance certificate / Foreign Exchange Settlement (FIRC) issued by a People's Bank of China-approved bank
Export services transaction list and service completion certificate (e.g., usage logs and server access records)
If any physical goods are bundled with the services: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) and Bill of Lading
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA conducts risk-based audits on export zero-rating claims. If zero-rating is claimed fraudulently or without complete substantiation, the STA will require repayment of all input VAT credits previously recovered, impose a late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day of the unrecovered tax, and levy administrative penalties ranging from 50% to 500% of the tax amount under the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law. In severe cases, criminal liability for tax fraud may arise under Article 204 of the Criminal Law, and the enterprise will be placed on the tax integrity blacklist, resulting in loss of future export zero-rating eligibility and enhanced scrutiny for subsequent fiscal periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible on the current account for trade in goods and services: the WFOE may receive and pay subscription fees for LegalTech SaaS under genuine contracts, and banks will register the transaction in SAFE's monitoring systems. However, the capital account remains strictly controlled. Equity injection from a Taiwan shareholder is categorized as foreign direct investment; it must be filed with the Ministry of Commerce and registered with SAFE before the remittance. The foreign currency capital must enter a designated FDI capital account at a Chinese domestic bank, and any settlement into RMB is restricted to the WFOE's approved operating purposes. Profit remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is permitted only after annual statutory audit, corporate income tax filing, and a declaration of the dividend distribution, and the bank verifies the relationship through the SAFE system. No mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds, but every inbound/outbound remittance must have a valid underlying transaction and, where exceeding the threshold, complete a foreign exchange declaration. This framework is stringent and supervisory, preventing an offshore EMI from acting as the sole treasury channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods trade, export proceeds must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange account within 90 days of customs declaration unless an extension is filed in SAFE's monitoring system; no fixed percentage must be sold to the state, but banks may urge settlement for balance-of-payments purposes. For service trade, including cloud contract automation, proceeds must be collected under contract and invoice and can remain in a domestic foreign currency account without mandatory conversion. The WFOE must report each transaction through the bank in the SAFE cross-border payments system.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Stripe is not a licensed Chinese banking institution and does not provide settlement accounts to mainland Chinese registered entities. Using Stripe directly as a merchant rail for the WFOE would violate Chinese payment administration and SAFE rules unless an offshore affiliate in a Stripe-supported jurisdiction is the actual merchant. Fintech EMIs such as Airwallex and Payoneer can support offshore collections through partner banks but cannot complete FDI capital registration, RMB basic account opening, tax payments, or profit remittance formalities. The WFOE must therefore maintain its treasury backbone in a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank. Viability rating: Low for direct onshore settlement; Medium only as an auxiliary offshore collection service for a non-China sales entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The WFOE's legal representative is generally required to appear physically at the bank branch in mainland China with the original business license, company seal, foreign investor registration documents, and personal identification. For a Taiwan legal representative, the Mainland Travel Permit for Taiwan Residents and valid entry record are mandatory. Remote consular proxy account opening is not accepted for an RMB Basic Deposit Account under PBOC account-management rules. If the legal representative cannot attend, the bank may accept an authorized signatory with a notarized board resolution and a notarized power of attorney, but the legal representative must still complete a video/telephone compliance interview and biometric identity confirmation where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan-based beneficial owner with political exposure or conflict-sensitive profile, combined with mainland China WFOE ownership, triggers enhanced due diligence for foreign money laundering and sanctions risks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved Foreign Investment Filing Certificate from the local Commerce bureau; SAFE FDI Foreign Exchange Registration Form; notarized UBO passport and Taiwan resident permit; signed politically-exposed-persons declaration; audited Taiwan shareholder financial statements; bank reference from a Taiwanese Tier-1 bank; corporate structure chart and complete shareholding register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No minimum paid-in capital and a cloud-only legaltech business model can present shell-company indicators, especially when revenues are collected via Stripe and credit cards from multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution fixing initial working capital; executed SaaS subscription agreements with e-signature audit logs; auditable revenue dashboard and invoicing ledger; office lease and workforce social-security records; monthly cash-flow forecast; software copyright and domain registration certificates; CPA confirmation of business substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI capital used for purposes outside the approved business scope or eventual repayment of shareholder loans creates unauthorised foreign-exchange settlement risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE-registered FDI capital account statement; board-approved capital-use budget tied to payroll, IT, rent, and statutory expenses; supplier contracts and invoices; no real-estate or equity-use undertaking; subsequent CPA certification that the capital was settled only through the bank's capital-projects monitoring system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border digital service revenue from global counterparties could be interpreted as disguised two-track settlement or unlicensed foreign-exchange operation without proper trade-in-service filing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual evidence for each counterparty, including master service agreements and statements of work; Stripe monthly merchant settlement reports; commercial invoices in each currency; SAFE service-trade foreign-exchange declaration forms; annual tax audit file confirming the WFOE's export service status under the relevant tax treaty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder should remit via SWIFT MT103 from a Taiwan bank to the WFOE's designated FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a Chinese Tier-1 bank. The remittance instruction must reference the SAFE FDI registration code and state the purpose as direct equity investment. After credit, the receiving bank completes the foreign exchange income registration, the CPA issues a capital verification report, and the WFOE files the verified record with SAFE and the local Commerce authority. The funds may then be settled into RMB solely for the approved operating purposes through the bank's capital-project monitoring system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for operational and service-trade disbursements is SWIFT MT103 backed by contract, invoice, and tax documentation. For goods-related settlement, a sight or usance Commercial Letter of Credit issued by a Chinese Tier-1 bank and confirmed by the counterparty's bank is permissible; Documentary Collections under D/P or D/A terms may be used for established trading partners. Each outbound remittance must be declared in the SAFE cross-border receipts and payments system, and service-trade payments above threshold require tax clearance and withholding tax certification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB/USD forward contracts with onshore banks under SAFE real-demand background verification
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for matching foreign-currency assets and liabilities
Plain vanilla options for hedging uncertain timing of subscription receivables in USD and EUR
Onshore nondeliverable forwards are not permissible for the WFOE; offshore CNH NDF may be used only by an offshore affiliate and cannot be settled through the domestic capital account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Disclosure Report (Annual Corporate Registration Renewal Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) / Provincial Administration for Market Regulation via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 to June 30 for the preceding calendar year (fixed window, not based on incorporation anniversary).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the window results in inclusion on the 'Abnormal Operations List' (经营异常名录). If the entity remains unrectified for 3 consecutive years, it is placed on the 'Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List' and may face administrative revocation of its business license, reputational damage, and restriction of legal representative rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audit and Filing of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) / AMR / Foreign Exchange Administration (SAFE) via annual report attachment or separate request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be completed and filed with the AMR as part of the annual information report no later than June 30; tax filing deadline of May 31 generally requires audited figures before the EIT settlement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to attach or submit the audit report where legally required may render the AMR annual report incomplete and cause the entity to be listed as abnormal; misstatement can trigger penalties under the Accounting Law (up to RMB 100,000 for entities and RMB 5,000 to RMB 50,000 for responsible individuals).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory for all Foreign-Invested Enterprises, including WFOEs, regardless of size, under PRC Foreign Investment Law and related implementation rules. In addition, an independent audit is required if the company exceeds any of: (1) annual operating revenue above RMB 100 million (approx. USD 14 million); (2) total assets above RMB 50 million (approx. USD 7 million); (3) staff headcount above 300; (4) if the entity is applying for equity transfer, merger, division, capital reduction, or dissolution; (5) if required by a bank, shareholder, or foreign exchange administration. The audit must be conducted by a licensed PRC CPA firm and issued in Chinese.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_: Chinese Accounting Standards (CAS / PRC GAAP), which are based on and converge with IFRS for large and medium-sized entities; small-scale enterprises may apply the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, but full CAS is generally applied for WFOEs. For IFRS or US GAAP consolidated reporting purposes, a dual report or IFRS-basis supplementary report may be prepared in addition to the statutory CAS report.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China has a centralized Beneficial Ownership Information Management System (BOI) effective 1 November 2024, requiring companies to submit a Beneficial Owner Information Report to the AMR. Initial filing must occur within 30 days after the entity becomes a reporting company; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the change. There is no annual standalone renewal cycle, but the annual AMR enterprise information report must reflect accurate equity and control information as of December 31 of the reporting year. Failure to file BOI or update changes within 30 days can result in fines up to RMB 10,000 for the company and RMB 5,000 for responsible individuals; repeated or serious violations may trigger higher enforcement and compliance disqualification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Resolutions
Register of Chops / Seals (Company Chop Use Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 6,000 per year for a registered address in a Tier-1 PRC city (Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen) including corporate secretarial support; USD 600 to USD 2,500 per year in Tier-2 or Tier-3 cities; actual physical office leases are separate and not included.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 15,000 per year for a typical WFOE with annual revenue under USD 10 million, depending on asset size, transaction complexity, intercompany activity, and whether IFRS/US GAAP bridge or transfer pricing schedules are required.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under PRC law, a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is mandatorily subject to annual statutory audit regardless of thresholds, because it is a foreign-invested enterprise. In addition, independent certified CPA audits are statutorily required if any of the following quantitative triggers are met: balance sheet total assets exceeding RMB 50 million (approx. USD 7 million); annual operating revenue exceeding RMB 100 million (approx. USD 14 million); staff headcount exceeding 300 employees; or the entity undertakes capital reduction, equity transfer, merger, division, liquidation, or requests a tax refund or preferential treatment. The governing accounting framework is the Chinese Accounting Standards (CAS / PRC GAAP), which converges substantially with IFRS. For small enterprises, the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards may apply, but WFOE audits must be conducted by a licensed PRC CPA firm in accordance with Chinese Standards on Auditing (CSA).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Chinese Accounting Standards (CAS) / PRC GAAP; large- and medium-sized enterprises must apply the full CAS. IFRS or US GAAP may be used only for supplementary consolidated reporting to foreign shareholders; the statutory financial statements must be prepared under CAS and audited under Chinese Standards on Auditing (CSA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Regulations on the Management of Beneficial Ownership Information (effective 1 November 2024), all companies, including WFOEs, must submit Beneficial Owner Information Reports to the State Administration for Market Regulation (AMR). Initial submission must occur within 30 days of becoming a reporting entity; changes in beneficial ownership or share transfers must be reported to AMR within 30 days of the event. There is no separate annual renewal, but the annual enterprise information report must be consistent with the BOI filing. Failure to file accurately and within the 30-day window may result in a fine of up to RMB 10,000 for the company and RMB 5,000 for responsible individuals, with more severe penalties for non-compliance and enforcement actions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 6,000 per year for a registered office address in a Tier-1 PRC city (Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen) with compliance mailbox services; USD 600 to USD 2,500 per year in Tier-2 or Tier-3 cities; actual physical office lease excluded.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 15,000 per year for a typical WFOE with annual revenue under USD 10 million, depending on transaction volume, intercompany balances, and need for IFRS/US GAAP conversion.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise income tax is levied at a headline rate of 20%. No general tax holiday applies to a standard WFOE, but eligible legal-tech or cloud software research and development expenditures may be credited at 15% of the qualifying R&D amount under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, subject to a ceiling of 30% of the current-year tax payable. Free-trade-zone preferential rates are available only where the revenue is physically sourced from licensed free-zone operations and the entity maintains a free-zone registration. In addition, a 5% retained-earnings surtax is triggered when surplus is not distributed in the same year, making the effective rate dependent on dividend distribution policy and available R&D credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (Form 15) filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance e-Filing Portal for profit-seeking enterprise income tax, together with the related-party transaction disclosure schedule and audited financial statements.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with mandatory quarterly provisional tax prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual settlement return must be filed within five months after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year entity, the deadline is 31 May of the following year. Quarterly provisional prepayments are generally due by 30 June, 30 September and 30 December, respectively.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Gross operating revenue and non-operating income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate Taiwanese-source gross revenue, including cloud document automation subscriptions, e-signature transaction fees, legal contract generation revenue, and any non-operating income such as interest or foreign exchange gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Taiwan WFOE, all Taiwan-source service income must be recorded in gross Form 15 Box 1. Cross-border SaaS and e-signature service revenue is Taiwan-source when the customer is in Taiwan or the service is performed in Taiwan. Foreign customers using online portals do not automatically turn the income into foreign-source income; the entity should maintain contracts, IP location data, and server records to support the source classification and avoid understatement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Cost of goods sold and direct service cost
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to providing legal contract automation services, including cloud hosting fees, subcontracted software development, third-party legal content licensing, and direct labor of delivery engineers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany costs paid to foreign affiliates must be supported by an executed cost-sharing or service agreement, evidence of actual service, and an arm-s-length mark-up. If the Taiwan entity merely pays royalties or fees to a related offshore company without local substance, the deduction will be recharacterized or disallowed under Income Tax Act Article 43-1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated as Box 1 less Box 2, representing gross profit before operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The gross margin should align with the transfer pricing documentation. A margin below industry comparables will be scrutinized as a possible profit shift to related parties; prepare a benchmark study for the digital legal-tech / SaaS industry and retain supporting market comparables.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales, marketing, general administrative, research and development, depreciation, amortization, royalties, and other ordinary business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Qualifying R&D expenses should be separately listed to claim the 15% investment tax credit. Any management fees paid to a foreign parent require substantive evidence of benefit, actual activity, and no double-counting with royalty payments. A non-resident audit may be triggered if intercompany management fees exceed Taiwan payroll or if personnel substance is minimal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Non-operating income and non-operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report interest income, foreign exchange gains/losses, gain/loss on disposal of assets, and other incidental income or losses outside the main business scope.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign exchange differences must be realized and supported by bank statements and annual revaluation reports. Dividends or distributions received from foreign subsidiaries are not automatically exempt unless the participation-exemption conditions are met; where a foreign parent is the beneficial owner of the Taiwan WFOE, the taxable event for outbound distribution occurs only upon the Taiwan entity declaring a dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Net taxable income before tax credits and loss offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory net income after all adjustments, reconciled to the audited financial statements, before applying the loss carryforward and computing corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entity must attach the intercompany transaction disclosure form and identify all related-party transactions in local and foreign currency. A five-year loss carryforward is allowed only if the prior-year returns were filed on time and accounting records are complete. Non-resident shareholders cannot directly deduct Taiwan entity tax losses against their own foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax payable and final liability after credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of income tax at the headline rate, application of the R&D credit and foreign tax credit, deduction of provisional prepayments, and the final net tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend distribution withholding tax is not an expense nor an offset in Box 7; if the Taiwan entity pays a dividend to a non-resident parent, the 20% withholding tax must be separately negotiated and remitted using the applicable withholding statement. Treaty relief on the dividend must be filed before remittance; otherwise the local withholding agent is obligated to withhold the full statutory rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return by the statutory deadline subjects the taxpayer to statutory interest, an estimated assessment, and a late-payment surcharge under the Tax Collection Act of up to 15% of the unpaid tax. Under Income Tax Act Article 108, an additional penalty of up to 10% of the assessed tax may be imposed where the return is filed late after investigation. Under-reported taxable income is subject to a penalty of two times the underpaid tax under Income Tax Act Article 110, rising to three times for deliberate concealment or fraudulent evasion. Willful tax evasion is criminally punishable under Tax Collection Act Article 41 by imprisonment for no more than five years and a fine, with directors at risk of personal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on dividends distributed by a Taiwan resident company to a non-resident foreign enterprise without a Taiwan permanent establishment (PE); 21% applies to non-resident individual shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced withholding tax rate under a bilateral double tax treaty or the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement with Mainland China, the non-resident shareholder must (i) be the beneficial owner of the dividend; (ii) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the other jurisdiction for the year of distribution; (iii) file an advance withholding-tax application with the Taiwan tax authorities and the remitting company before the dividend distribution record date; (iv) demonstrate that no Taiwan PE effectively connects the dividend to Taiwan business activities; and (v) complete the beneficial-ownership declaration, including evidence of shareholder status, holding period, and substantive business existence. If approval is not granted before remittance, the full statutory 20% must be withheld, and a refund may be claimed by filing an amended withholding return with supporting treaty forms.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory Taiwan withholding tax rate for royalties and interest paid to a non-resident enterprise without a Taiwan PE is 20% for each income type. Under an applicable DTA or the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, interest and royalty withholding rates may be reduced, commonly to a treaty ceiling such as 7% or 10%, only after the recipient provides a TRC, a beneficial-ownership certificate, proof of use of the intellectual property or debt in the source jurisdiction, and confirmation that the income is not attributable to a Taiwan PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File transfer-pricing report must be prepared and maintained where annual related-party transactions exceed New Taiwan Dollars (NTD) 50 million for any single related-party transaction category or NTD 100 million in total cross-border related-party volume. A Master File is required where the Taiwan entity is part of a multinational group with consolidated annual revenue exceeding NTD 5 billion, and a Country-by-Country Report is triggered when the consolidated group revenue exceeds NTD 27 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan applies the economic-substance principle through Income Tax Act Article 43-1, the place-of-effective-management rules, and the general anti-avoidance doctrine. Although Taiwan does not issue statutory Economic Substance Regulations certificates, the WFOE must still maintain physical management, strategic decision-making, employees, technical capability, and Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Taiwan. For a legal-tech SaaS and e-signature automation business, CIGA includes product development, encryption-key management, platform hosting, contract execution and authentication, billing, and customer support. If these functions are performed offshore, the Taiwan tax authority may disregard the legal entity, reattribute profits to the foreign beneficial owner, deny treaty benefits, and impose additional withholding tax and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Revenue Suppression
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording Taiwan-source SaaS subscription and e-signature fees in a foreign affiliate or personal account, issuing fictitious intercompany invoices to inflate costs, or deliberately omitting online contract-automation revenues from Form 15 Box 1.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act Article 110, the underpaid tax is penalized at two times the amount understated; where deliberate fraud or concealment is established, the penalty is increased to three times the underpaid tax. Tax Collection Act Article 41 additionally imposes criminal imprisonment of up to five years and a fine for willful evasion, and statutory interest runs on all outstanding tax liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the WFOE is found to be a mere instrumentality of its directors. Directors who signed false tax returns or approved fictitious invoices may be jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the unpaid tax and penalties. The tax authority may impose an exit ban / travel blacklisting under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act until the tax is secured, and directors face criminal imprisonment of up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Tax Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm-s-length intercompany royalty, management-fee, or cloud-service contracts with a foreign parent, using an excessive mark-up without benchmarking, failing to prepare or file a Local File when the statutory threshold is exceeded, or omitting the related-party transaction disclosure schedule in the annual return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 43-1 empowers the tax authority to recharacterize intercompany transactions to arm-s-length pricing, add the adjusted profit to taxable income, deny the related deductions, and impose a penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax. Interest accrues from the original due date of the underpayment, and repeated violations may be treated as intentional tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved intercompany pricing without transfer pricing documentation or signed financial statements containing misstated intercompany transactions can be held personally liable under Company Act Article 23 for damages caused to the company. In aggravated cases, directors are named in tax enforcement proceedings with property seizure and travel blacklisting, and may be criminally prosecuted if the pricing arrangement is structured to conceal profit-shifting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure / Treaty Abuse / AML Beneficial Ownership Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Taiwan WFOE as a paper company with no real office, no employees, no software development, no hosting infrastructure, and no substantive Board decision-making anywhere in Taiwan, while routing profits to an offshore affiliate solely to access DTA relief and avoid Taiwan-source taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will deny treaty relief retroactively, re-instate the full 20% withholding tax on all outbound distributions, assess additional penalty and interest, and may disregard the legal entity under the substantive-taxation doctrine. If the structure is used to move illicit funds or conceal the true beneficial owner, the Money Laundering Control Act and the Company Act beneficial-ownership filing rules impose separate penalties, including monetary fines and criminal liability for nominee directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee or shadow directors face piercing of the corporate veil with personal civil liability for the company's unpaid withholding tax and penalties. Travel blacklisting is available to compel settlement. If the shell arrangement is tied to money laundering, directors face criminal prosecution with imprisonment of up to seven years, asset forfeiture, and disqualification from serving as directors of any Taiwan company.
